subject: Re: Follow-up: Long-context evals & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up + proposed plan for long-context evals

Hi Joe —

Great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking through Acme's summarization pipeline and the examples you shared. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get you a concrete evaluation that answers the truncation and fidelity questions: 

Recap of needs
- Ingest long technical documents (20–200k tokens) and produce robust extractive/abstractive summaries for downstream search and KB ingestion.
- Concerned about truncation behavior and whether the model preserves critical facts across the long context window.
- Need to compare latency/cost tradeoffs vs. quality (you mentioned a soft SLA of <2s per 1k tokens for tail p95).

Recommended evaluation approach
1) Long-context fidelity eval: run a set of ~200 staged documents through (attached prompt set) to measure information retention, hallucination rate, and chunking/summarization consistency.
2) Truncation stress tests: incremental context lengths (8k, 32k, 64k, 128k) to observe where summarization fidelity drops and what failure modes look like.
3) Latency/cost profiling: run at representative batch sizes and expected concurrency to estimate per-token compute and tail latencies.

Initial model recommendations
- redwood-long-32k-v2 (fast, tuned for long-context tasks) — good baseline for fidelity vs performance
- redwood-xlarge-70b-q4 (quantized) — higher quality, better factuality on abstractive summaries, higher cost
- redwood-encoder-embedding-1 (for downstream similarity checks and QA reranking)

Attachments and links
- Attached: acme_long_context_promptset_v1.csv (sample prompt templates + expected outputs)
- Redwood eval template: redwood_eval_template.pdf (format we use to report metrics + examples)
- Benchmark link: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/long-context/2026-acme (we will upload results here)

Next steps (proposed)
- We can run a free pilot eval on your dataset (up to 200 docs) next week. Required from your side: sample documents (S3 link or Drive) and a short prioritized checklist of what counts as a regression for you.
- I'll loop Logan (SE) to scope the technical run and share a MAP + timeline.

Would Wednesday 10/14 for a 30-min kickoff work?

Best —
Marissa Cole

Hi Joe —

Great questions — quick answers below, plus a proposed MAP so procurement can see timelines: 

1) Truncation/streaming behavior
- For very long docs (>>32k) we recommend one of two approaches depending on the use case:
  a) Hierarchical summarization (chunk -> summarize -> synthesize): preserves fidelity and is cost-effective, but you need to tune chunk size and overlap.
  b) KV/prefix caching + sliding-window attention (available on our dedicated/private deployments): better for real-time passes where you need exact token-addressability but more expensive.
- Failure modes to watch for: dropped context (facts in earlier sections not referenced), repetition when synthesis is naive, and boundary artifacts where entities are split across chunk boundaries. Our eval template flags these and provides examples.

2) Ballpark pilot cost (200 docs)
- redwood-long-32k-v2: ~ $800-$1,200 (depends on avg doc length and batching)
- redwood-xlarge-70b-q4: ~ $2,400-$3,200
- Embedding/reranking runs: additional ~$150
(we'll refine once you share size distribution and concurrency expectations)

3) Data isolation and legal
- Pilot data is isolated and not used to train models by default. We can provide a data processing addendum and redwood-nontraining-nda.pdf if you need it. For full Private deployments we offer customer-managed KMS.

MAP (proposed)
- 10/12: Acme shares sample dataset + priority regression list (you)
- 10/14: Kickoff (30m) — scope run and finalize model choices (Marissa + Logan + Joe)
- 10/15–10/20: Pilot runs and metric collection (Logan + Infra)
- 10/21: Results review + recommended next steps (Marissa + Joe)

I've attached the eval template again and uploaded a benchmark folder — we'll drop intermediate results to the Drive link. Logan, if you can confirm the runtime configuration we should use for the pilot (batch sizes, sequence lengths, quant settings), that would be great.

Thanks —
Marissa

Quick internal note after confirming infra for the pilot:
- Runtime: use the long-context optimized runtime with kernel selection enabled. Start with 32k context runs, then expand to 64k and 128k for the stress tests.
- Chunking: use 4k chunk size with 20% overlap for hierarchical summarization; this reduces boundary artifacts in our experience.
- Metrics we'll collect: ROUGE-L, factuality score (QA-based), hallucination count, token-cost, p95 latency.
- Access: I'll provision a short-lived S3 ingest bucket and a read-only Drive folder for Acme results.
